item.title: It's Medicare open enrollment time. Here's what you need to know
item.description: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.

item.title: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
item.description: The money will go to thousands of people who have been or will be diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma – a blood cancer linked to the herbicide.

item.title: Philadelphia neonatologist Joanna Parga-Belinkie on keeping babies safe from measles
item.description: Amid ongoing measles outbreaks, Philadelphia neonatologist Joanna Parga-Belinkie talks with NPR's Scott Simon about how she keeps infants too young for the vaccine safe.

item.title: For some patients, psychedelic treatment brings new troubles in its aftermath
item.description: Psychedelics could transform mental health care, but some advocates and researchers say there needs to be more focus on the minority of people with persistent troubles after using these drugs.

item.title: These women are Nepal's unsung heroes: shattered by the floods yet helping survivors
item.description: The floods of August took many lives, destroyed homes, hospitals and schools. Aid workers are taking up the hard work of rebuilding communities that suffered — even though they, too, saw great losses.

item.title: As overdose deaths fall, White House makes misleading claims about who deserves credit
item.description: In a statement celebrating the historic drop in drug deaths, the White House pointed to successes since President Trump took office. In fact, the biggest progress happened under the Biden administration.

item.title: The off-and-on switch for U.S. aid leads to a cliffhanger for Zambia and Zimbabwe
item.description: After dismantling the United States Agency for International Development, the Trump administration is restarting foreign aid. In Zambia and Zimbabwe, there are different approaches but similar worries.

item.title: Public health expert reacts to latest measles milestone
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with Dr. Ashish Jha, senior fellow at Harvard's Belfer Center and former White House coronavirus czar, about the news that the U.S. has lost its measles elimination status.
